utterances.text: What about the protection by the military police, health care? Did you manage to organise all that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes. There were some medical interventions and we had a doctor amongst us, we also had a nurse and a paramedic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When you mentioned Petkovic and Halilovic delegation, was UNPROFOR with them as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think we are at a point where some dates would be helpful. Some of these events took place over a number of weeks and I fear that at the moment, this is all being presented in such a fashion that it sounds like it's all happening in the course of a day or two. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, would you please make that clear for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've been following the transcript and it seems that everything is clear. We are talking about the 17th of April and the witness replied to my question regarding the soldiers, regarding the civilians, and then he said that on the 4th of May, based on the Petkovic-Halilovic agreement, there was an exchange of civilians. I believe that this is all clear. I'm just asking the witness whether there were international community representatives accompanying that Petkovic-Halilovic delegation. I'm talking about the civilians and the witness answered yes, but this hasn't been recorded. So I am repeating my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were representatives of the international community in Sovici on the 4th of May, together with Mr. Petkovic and Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes, there was UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were there any objections on their part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: No. There were no objections, either on the part of the civilians or on the part of the international community, or on the part of Mr. Petkovic and Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please assist the Chamber and tell them, on the 17th of April, how long did it take one to get from Sovici to Ljubuski? Do you know that personally? How long does -- would it take a bus to get from Sovici to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: It's a very hard for me to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I believe it took four or five hours by bus, because the road was in a very bad state of repairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was there a road across Risovac? Was that a normal asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: No. The road from Sovici to Risovac and on towards Posusje was a macadam road. It wasn't very easy to travel on that road for any type of vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm just trying to paint a picture for the Chamber. Can you please now tell me -- tell me whether you know Zijad Kladusak and if you do know him, can you tell us where he was, which unit was he a member of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes, I know Mr. Kladusak. As far as I know, he and his brother, Nijaz, were members of the HVO. He is of Bosniak ethnicity. He was a member of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What was his duty in the HVO? Do you perhaps know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I think he was just a foot soldier. That was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: His occupational duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm going to show you document D1/412. Can you please locate his name, find his name in this document, and see whether that corresponds to the truth? Can you please look at the page and tell me whether you have been able to find his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes. There is his name here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what does it say here? What is his military occupation or specialty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: He is a shooter, a sniper-shooter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What kind of weapons would he have as a shooter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, because I -- I've -- I never did that, but I believe he was given an automatic rifle. I believe that was the type of weapon he carried.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you ever see anybody beating or harassing or maltreating the prisoners, including him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: No. Nobody harassed or ill-treated BH Army soldiers, and that would apply to him as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Some witnesses have said that they were harassed. For example Witness AF, Witness Y. They claimed that they had been beaten and ill-treated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Nobody harassed or ill-treated them in Sovici, for the brief period of time that they were there. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is there any special reason why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: That's how things were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What I'm saying is these were your neighbours. Where were your people at the time? We have heard so many different things in this courtroom. That's why I called you. You were there. I wanted to hear from you. You're under oath.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: The local HVO members would never muster force to ill-treat these people, and to my knowledge, no other HVO soldiers ill-treated any of the prisoners either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We heard a testimony according to which you wanted to hang a prisoner whose pseudonym was Y. That's what that witness testified. That you wanted to hang him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: That is nothing but a blunt lie and it is absolutely inconceivable but -- that anybody would have as much as thought something like that, let alone attempt it, to do that, so I really don't know why anybody would say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you give a speech to the lined-up members of the BH Army? Some witnesses claimed you delivered a speech and in that speech, you told them that they were arrested for crimes against Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I never delivered a speech. It was not possible to deliver any such speeches. It was impossible. It was inconceivable. There were no conditions in place for anybody to deliver any speeches like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The school in Sovici, does it have a gym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: No, it doesn't have a gym. It's a very small, tiny school building, very poorly built, and it doesn't have a gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I am asking you that because some witnesses told us that they were taken to the gym of that school and that they were ill-treated there. Are there any offices on the second floor of that school building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What is on the second floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: As far as I know, there are just two class rooms on the second floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you, because some witnesses said that there were offices on the second floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: No, there are no offices there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well, then. Can you tell us anything else about that day, the 17th of April? We are coming to the break. I have a few questions about Doljani. So let's finish with the Sovici story. Do you have anything else to say about that day? Let me ask you. On the 17th of April, in Sovici, did you see the man whose nickname is Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I didn't see anybody. I just had a man introduced to me as Tuta Gmici and he was the commander of one of these units but that's a customary, that's a very usual nickname. There was a guy in Doljani whose last name was Tutis, his first name was Ivan and his nickname was also Tuta. So Tuta is not such an unusual nickname in that neck of the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you see Mladen Naletilic in Sovici on the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: No. I didn't see Mr. Naletilic on the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you see or did you meet any members of the Convicts Battalion in Sovici on the 17th of April? Are you familiar with that unit at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I didn't see members of the Convicts Battalion on that day in Sovici. I heard of them later on but that was a bit later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We'll come to that. We had a testimony here, according to which Mr. Naletilic had introduced himself to an old man by the name of Rafo Cvitkovic, in the presence of Witness Y and that's why Witness Y thought that this indeed was Mr. Naletilic. You mentioned Mr. Rafo Cvitkovic in your testimony today. Is there just one person by that name or are there more than one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: As far as I know, there is just one Rafo Cvitkovic, and he wasn't there that day, because I had bumped into him two days earlier in Prozor, in a place called Gmici where he was with his son and his daughter-in-law in their family house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe the time has come for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please return -- repeat the name of the place where that Mr. Cvitkovic was at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: The name of the place is Gmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you spell that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: is where I slept on the night between the 14th and the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. It is 1.00 this is our time for the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you indeed think that it is the time for the break, I will be very brief after the break. Just have a few more questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will adjourned until 3.00 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we are informed that the Prosecutor would like to address the bench. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please, Mr. President -- I know we have a witness pending but I'm learning that it's better not to let these things slide along. So it's better for me to raise them now. First of all, Mr. President, in relationship to the document matter that rose before the break with Mr. Prelec, I do have obviously I have not had it translated yet but I do have for the Chamber's information and for Defence counsel, the list of 86 names which I'll provide to the usher now and ask her assistance in it providing one to each Defence team and one to each of the Judges, please. I have requested a translation, Mr. President, and as soon as the translation is available, certainly it will be provided to you. Secondly, Mr. President, I need to raise an issue about the -- what has come to be called the blue ink diary. Since that is an original document in the sense of being written in blue ink and a journal and not a xerox copy, and because we would like to be able to verify some translation matters, I need the Chamber's assistance, I think since the original is now in the possession of the Registry, could the Chamber please make some arrangements whereby perhaps all three parties, the Prosecution and each Defence team could be provided with something that would be considered an official copy or certificated copy of the journal so that there could be no dispute about that? We don't it particularly want to take it back because of the chain of custody issues ourselves and because of the issues that have been raised about the typed version or this version, we would like to have a -- what the Court considers an official copy taken from the blue ink journal if we could please ask your assistance on that, Mr. President, and with all respect, reasonably as quickly as those arrangements can be made so that we can make further verifications on that. I thought, Mr. President, on that as well, I need to alert the Chamber that after Mr. Idrizovic was excused last week, he had said that he had previously provided a copy of his -- copy of his copy of the handwritten diary and, Mr. President, it's the Prosecutor position or submission that that's a mistake. We had a typed version that he had given us. We have asked Mr. Idrizovic and have made arrangements, I'm just telling the Chamber so that again operating in complete transparency that we have asked, made arrange documents obtain that -- a copy from Mr. Idrizovic of his handwritten version in Bosnia-Herzegovina this week. And simply so the Chamber knows that, we are going to make those efforts to do that. Finally, Mr. President, there was one additional document, and since we are quickly coming to the end of the evidence, in addition to the documents I gave the Chamber this morning, about the translation, some that were pending translation, the Prosecution is prepared, and I see that I've -- unfortunately I've pulled it out and left it in another binder, when we played the "Juri and Boban" song to the Chamber, the Court may recall and provided -- actually we didn't provide a new transcript because we had used Defence Exhibit D1/277, when that was played in court it was pointed out to us by people who heard the song that the text that was provided and the translation were not completely accurate. Therefore, we have provided a new text and translation, which is in the bundle of rebuttal documents, Mr. President, and again, if you'll allow me, -- here it is. 961.1, I think there is at least one line of text that was previously omitted and there were a couple of words that we submit were different, and again, Mr. President, because I don't want to get caught before the end of the evidence, we would like to tender that exhibit, P/961.1, as a corrected text translation of that song. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. First of all, could I be provided with a copy which is in sequence? Because I have seven blank pages. This is what I have just received from the Prosecutor. From number 5 to 25, page 5 to page 25. The one that has just been provided with 86 names. This is Exhibit 314.3. We have just been provided with it. So from page 5 to page 25, I don't have a single name on these pages. I have three absolutely blank pages. You can see that for yourselves. And from number 34 up to number 43, another four blank pages. So I would like the full document to be provided. And finally, we listened to Mr. Idrizovic's testimony very carefully and I questioned him and then the Judge Clark. We know what his responses were and they have been recorded in the transcript. If the Prosecutor think that is something is wrong, that's his opinion. The witness testified here and replied to my questions and those of Judge Clark, and he replied to our questions under oath, so I really don't understand what it means to say to -- to provide other copies, to re-examine these things. It's very easy to verify the transcript and to check what he said. I think that doing anything else would be quite superfluous. As far as the song is concerned, the Prosecutor first claimed it was identical. He said he wasn't interested in the words, because Defence counsel had provided the words and that he accepted that those were the words of the song. Now I see that yet again he thinks that something is not quite correct and I don't know how far this will go. I fear that this may simply not end. And we have that CD too. We could have played it but out much respect for your decision, we don't want to raise these matters. Once I've been provided with a complete document, P314.3, we will make our position clear, but at the moment, given what I have just seen, I have nothing against the Trial Chamber examining this and having the Trial Chamber reach a decision. But I think the most important thing is to have a full, a complete document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, we were also provided a document which seems to me several pages missing. Would you please give us some explanation about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. To avoid any allegations of impropriety, we have given you exactly the document as it exists in our files. And you'll see on the second page, which is empty other than the fact that it has a separate ERN number and a separate Zagreb stamp at the top of the page, that's exactly how the document exists in our files. So we have not -- we have not removed any pages, I don't know why the empty extra pages were there. If it was done when the Zagreb archive copied the document and gave it to us, but we copied it exactly as it exists in the records of the OTP. And it contains those pages. It's apparent, Mr. President, that it goes from number 5 on the first page, the pages do have to be put back into order, as best as possible, but that's the document as it exists, Mr. President. I don't think it was up to the Prosecutor it to rearrange the document. That's the document that exists. As to Mr. Idrizovic, Your Honour, I don't know what else to tell the Chamber. I realise that there -- I know full well what the testimony was at the end of his examination, at the end of his testimony, whether it was a translation error or whether he was in error, I don't know. This raises one of those situations. All I can do is advise the Chamber that according to our records, according to the OTP's records we did not receive a copy of the handwritten diary from Mr. Idrizovic. The Chamber can do with that as it wants but I've now advised the Chamber so there can be no question about that. Thirdly, concerning the song, again, Mr. President, I'm in the Chamber's hands. The Chamber is welcome to play the tape which is in evidence to any of the professional translation staff. It doesn't have any anyone associated with the Prosecution. In fact I would invite to you have it played to one of the translation booths completely separate, independent of the translation -- of the Prosecution, and I think you will hear that, in fact, there was some text that had been omitted and not properly translated. But again, the Chamber can deal with it as you will. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you. As for the translation of the document, P314.3, we will not consider to admit it into evidence until we have the translation of that document, because we have to know what this document is about. Secondly, I would like to entrust Madam Registrar to make so-called official photocopy of that blue ink diary and distribute it to both parties. Thirdly as for the translation of the song, this Trial Chamber will ask the official translator of this Tribunal to check the translation of that song. If we want to have it admitted into the evidence. Having said that, Madam Usher, could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, we'll just wait for this to finish. Let's try and see what happened in Doljani on the 17th and 18th and after that. Were there BH Army members, were there civilians there? What took place there? Do you have any personal knowledge of the events that took place there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes. As I have already said, the civilians, the Bosniak civilians and the BH Army members from Doljani, in the evening and in the course of the day on the 17th, and on the 18th, they started leaving Doljani. They started leaving Doljani in the night. And on the 18th, in the course of the day, there was no one, as far as we knew, of Bosniak nationality in Doljani. According to what people said, they went to Jablanica and apparently their people ordered them to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And was there any fighting between the HVO and the BH Army? Was anyone captured there, perhaps somewhere around Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: No. There was no fighting in Doljani, not in the centre of the place itself but on the 18th, some Bosniaks who were elderly people were detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, on the 19th or on the 20th or later on, did BH Army members surrender? Were there any members in the hills?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes. There were various groups of Bosniaks who were found in the surrounding hills. They were returned to Doljani and to Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know who brought them there, where they were taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I think that -- well, maybe I know two out of five or six of them, Kovac was brought in, I think, and Skender, Denis, I think these two men were brought in. They were taken to Doljani. They were taken to the fish farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: They were sent -- Skender, I think he was a minor and he went up to where the civilians were and the military police took charge of the others -- of the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who took -- who brought them in, those two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I don't know exactly but they were HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Would you be so kind to tell us, to tell this Trial Chamber, whether the name Alojz Rados means anything to you. Do you know this person and if you do, where do you know him from? What was he? What did he do? If he was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes. I know that name. I don't know that man very well but I do know him by sight. I know that he worked and that he was in the HVO. As far as I know, his duties included health and the organisation of health care. He was a -- I think a -- part of the medical staff. I know that he worked around Jablanica and was involved in humanitarian care, humanitarian protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could Madam Registrar now provide Exhibit D1/413 and could it be shown to those present in the courtroom? Have a look at the Croatian version now. Try and see if you can find his name on that list and if you can -- what does it say at the beginning of the document? Can you tell me that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: It says, "Platoon, department for technical maintenance" and at the end the medical department, and under number 21, it says medical orderly. Alojz Rados from Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It hasn't entered into the transcript, what it says at the beginning of the document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: It says, "Quartermaster platoon."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know what sort of work he did as a medical orderly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning, while he was in Jablanica, I think that he worked for a volunteer association, the Croatian Catholic Volunteer Association. I think that that was the name. He obtained medical supplies and distributed them to those who needed it and later on, when he was in Doljani, in that medical clinic, and when he worked there as a medical orderly, he assisted there, he helped a doctor who worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know the name of that doctor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Vladtko Ljuban, I think, that was the doctor for a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Krsnik, could you furnish me with some information about this document? I mean the source of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber who provided me with this document, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Salgolj, Mr. Dravko Salgolj, the Brigade commander, the Herceg Stjepan Brigade commander. He did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you're a member of the police but someone from the army or you, if you wanted to leave Sovici or Doljani, did you have to have authorisation from the competent command to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes. Anyone who moved a bit further afield, or who was leaving the territory of the municipality, had to have some form of authorisation, it depend on the person concerned. If it was a soldier, then the soldier had to have authorisation from his commander. And if it was a civilian, then he had to have authorisation from his superiors, or in my case, I, as a police commander, I had permanent authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'll now show you document D1/438. It's a document that I was given by the Prosecutor so have a look at that document. Tell me, is there anything that is familiar to you in this document? Naturally, have a look at the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I hope that you have this document in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is this a permission, as it been issued by a commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's the usual kind of permission that you would receive in order to travel. It was necessary to have it in order to travel and so that one could know where a certain person was going.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So did this mean that the person concerned could be absent from his unit for a month or for however long it says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes, with this permission it was possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Calls for pure speculation, Mr. President, the witness has provided no foundation that he's ever even seen this document before. Only thing he has said is that people have to have such a document in their possession for freedom of movement purposes. There is absolutely nothing on this document that would indicate that the person actually travelled during that time, and unless counsel can provide some foundation of personal knowledge, I object to speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you may ask some questions along this line, to lay some foundations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I've been concerned for the last five minutes or so, this witness said that he only knew Alojz Rados by sight and yet he's purporting to give fairly detailed information about Mr. Rados's movements. That's one concern I have. The other concern I have is that you then stated to this witness that he was a member of the police. I thought he was a Judge in the misdemeanours court and that he said that the police station that he was in charge of wasn't a police station as such, it just issued certificates or something. I'm a little confused it's not clear to me, A, the source of this person's information on Mr. Rados and secondly, how he is a policeman suddenly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this will all be redacted so we hope we haven't caused any damage, any harm. So this has been his testimony from the very start. He was quite specific as to what he was during certain periods of time. I was just asking a general sort of question. Nothing else. You'll draw your own conclusions but all I want to know is whether such permission was necessary regardless of the name that you find on the permission, on the authorization. The name is interesting for me because the Prosecutor provided me with this document but I'm interested in this authorisation and not in the person himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, but Mr. Krsnik, you have to ask some questions to this witness whether he personally saw this permission, this document, or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my questions, I hope, are very clear. I'm asking from this witness to tell me whether such authorisations were the only valid ones for those who wanted to leave their units. That is all I am asking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Only such approvals or authorisations authorised a soldier or anybody else it to travel, to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Why? Where did he have to show such an authorisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Firstly he had to be recorded with the unit, and secondly, he would have to show that to a police checkpoints or on the border, the police control or on the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I believe I was absolutely clear. Let's move on then. We can go back into open session, Your Honours. Can you please assist the Chamber and tell us: Did you ever, on the 17th, 18th, the 19th or the 20th, did you ever see Mr. Naletilic or members of the Convicts Battalion in Doljani? If the answer is yes, can you tell us when, why, what did they do there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes. On the 19th of April, 1993, I saw Mr. Naletilic in Doljani, and I saw a few members of the Convicts Battalion, and that is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How far away were you from him? Did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I didn't talk to him. He was across the road from the command, across the road from the fish farm, from the water. I didn't talk to him but I was about 3 or four metres away from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How tall are you approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: 189, 189 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And can you tell us the height of Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: He is some -- by 20 centimetres shorter than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what was the colour of his hair at the time, what was the colour of his beard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: At the time, he had black hair, black beard, a few grey hairs, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We had some witnesses saying that he had blond hair and blond beard. That's why I ask you this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: He didn't say blond, he said grey.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I studied the testimonies. The witness Y said that he negotiated with a -- the man with blond hair and reddish beard and the way we translate this, it transpires as a person with a blond hair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, I thought, Mr. Krsnik, I thought you were talking about the man who very recently gave evidence. That is why it was fresh in my mind. I stand corrected. I have no idea what I said but I thought you were talking about a very recent witness, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are drawing to an end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know what the purpose was of Mr. Naletilic's visit to Doljani? How long did he stay there and what did the Convicts Battalion do in Doljani at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I understand that the men came because two of the members of the Convicts Battalion had died.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How did the Convicts Battalion arrive in Doljani? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I believe that the battles were taking place in the hills from Sovici to Pasje Stijene, Bacina, Pomina [phoen] and towards Tovarnica, and towards Kosna Luka settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So does that mean that from the mountain of Pomina, they descended to Kosna Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I don't know the exact route but that would make sense, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes. How long did they stay there and how long did Mr. Naletilic stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I don't know exactly but for a very short period of time, until they took the bodies of the fallen soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did they then leave and did they ever return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes, they left and they never returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Kindly, please, look at the document 333, Prosecution number P333. Did you ever see this document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: No. I never saw this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I know this person by the name, but I don't recognise his signature, this is not his signature. I know this man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems that we don't have that document at our hands. Is it possible to put this document on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Can you put the English version on the ELMO? [In English] Sorry, Your Honour, excuse me, I didn't know that you didn't have this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please put the Croatian version on the ELMO as well? Because the English version does not bear the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm going to show you the Exhibit D1/439. I have obtained the signature of this gentleman. Can you please look at the -- this signature? This was a document signed before the Court in Siroki Brijeg. Do you recognise this signature? Is this the person's signature, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes. To my knowledge, this is the signature, and this is the person whose signature this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name Cikota? Do you know what that person looked like, i.e. how tall was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I never saw that man, but according to my knowledge, according to what other people told me, he was the commander of the Convicts Battalion, and I know he died.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did anybody tell you how tall he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I know that he was strongly built and rather tall. I don't know how tall he was because I never saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] Okay, okay, okay, okay. [Interpretation] I am just checking to see whether I had forgotten to ask you something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Good try.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I really want to help everyone. If I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's not the way to do it but it was a good try.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I will now hand you over to my learned friend. I wanted to ask you a few questions about Mr. Rados since you said you knew -- know him but I will leave to my learned friend. Thank you for coming here. Thank you for assisting us. I apologise for having taken so much time. I'm not feeling too well. That's why it has taken me so long to examine you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning -- sorry, good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: [no interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm guilty. Could we please have this redacted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This is not the first day of the trial. You have to bare this in mind. We will have that redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You're not guilty for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think everyone in this courtroom, including the Judges have violated this at one time or another. My apology. And the redaction, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, you have to remember the principle of tu quoque.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Touche, Mr. President and could we go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you said in your testimony that a man named -- sir, you said that a man named Zajko Sihirlic, and excuse me if I mispronounce that, was the assistant of a man named Safet Idrizovic. What do you base that on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I base this on what I know, because Sihirlic is from Doljani and I know that he helped Mr. Idrizovic in conducting his affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, during what period of time, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, while I was still in Jablanica, and I also know that Mr. Sihirlic would present himself at the checkpoint, even before the open conflict. I believe that it was on the 16th that he came to the checkpoint below Doljani. That may not be correct but this is what I have been told.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you give us some specifics, sir, as to what basis you have, did you have, did you attend a meeting with the two of them where Mr. Sihirlic acted as an assistant? Can you give us some specifics as to why you believe that he was the assistant to Mr. Idrizovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I saw him at certain meetings and I also saw him in the command of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: During 1992, early 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, how early in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Up to mid-March.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, going to the 17th, 18th and 19th of April of 1993, sir, despite your testimony so far, it's not clear to me what were you doing during that time? Were you moving about among the fighting? Did you take up a position somewhere? What were you doing during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, 1993, I was in Doljani, in the police station, which is some 700 to 800 metres away from the battalion command, and the name of the building is the old community centre. I was there all the time up to noon or somewhat later, when I left for Sovici, as I've already said in my previous testimony. So I didn't take part anywhere as a soldier. I just performed my usual tasks and duties, as far as I could, as best as I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, since I've unfortunately caused a problem once already, just to be very safe in this area I would prefer that we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, we are returning to public session so I just caution you again that when you give your answers, if you could be careful about saying anything that might tend to identify you and if we need to we will go back to private session. But on this document, sir, and I think there is nothing about the document or the answers, I think, that would identify you, if I heard you correctly you say that this -- you thought that this document came from Mr. Salgolj, and I'm sure I'm probably saying that wrong, S-A-L-G-O-L-J. How do you know that's where this document came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Mr. Salgolj gave this to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Seven or eight days ago when I was in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree with me, as I've been reminded by the Defence on many occasions, this document has no letterhead, no date, no author, no signature, no stamp? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I can say that this document is a possible document but as to its authenticity, that is for you to assess.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: A couple of questions. You've mentioned in reference to the first page, or either in the Croatian language or in the English version, but in any event, person number 18, I believe you said on direct examination, that this described person 18 as a sniper. Now, isn't it correct, sir, that in contrast to that, if we look at the person numbered 13, number 13 is described as a sniper, at least that's the translation that we've been given; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I didn't say, and I didn't confirm, that the person under number 18 was a sniper. I said that the person under number 18 was a shooter. This -- there is an important distinction to be made here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Do you know what operator "PM" stands for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I think that means a light machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did I understand you to say, sir, that concerning the HVO actions at Sovici-Doljani in mid-April, 1993, there was no overall HVO commander? Simply had different units running around the country side with no coordination? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was not a single commander but the units that were there, as far as I know, they coordinated their action.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, how do you know that? You've told us what you were doing on the 17th, 18th and 19th of April so how do you know that they coordinated their actions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Mr. Groznica told me that this was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You said that no one at Sovici-Doljani mistreated the Muslim prisoners. Is that again just based on what you've been told?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: As far as I know, no one was maltreated and to the extent that I was there, I didn't see any one being maltreated and I was never told that anyone had been maltreated, neither soldiers nor civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During those three days we have talked about so far, could you tell the Judges, if you could add it all together, how many minutes or hours were you actually at a location where Muslims prisoners were? 15 minutes, half an hour, 45 minutes? How long did you actually yourself physically see any gathering of Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: What day are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Any of those days. How about the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: On the 17th, if you're asking me about a specific location, I was present for half an hour. If you're talking about a specific location on the road then it was half an hour but I also said that I slept there until the morning, until 7.00 or 8.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, are you suggesting that while were you sleeping, that you had your eye also on Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I think it's quite clear. I think you're able to understand what I did on the 17th. But if necessary, I shall go over it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let's go to the 18th. How much time on the 18th of April did you actually spend in the presence of any Muslim men who had been taken prisoner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: On the 18th, I wasn't in the presence of any prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How about the 19th, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: On the 19th, I only saw, as I have already said, a small group in Doljani that set off in the direction of Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And approximately how long did you observe this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Well, that was while I was there for a brief period, on the 19th. It was 10 to 20 minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. You said on your direct examination that in connection with questions about whether you delivered some sort of speech around the 17th or April -- excuse me, 17th or 18th of April, 1993, at the Sovici school, you said something -- there was no -- to the effect there was no place, there was no circumstance for delivering a speech. My question, sir, is what kind of a place was required in order to make a speech?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: When I said that, according to the information I had, the soldiers, the BH Army soldiers were in the school. That's what I meant when I said there was no possibility. They were in the premises of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct that the men were brought outside in front of the school and a speech was made at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I personally didn't give any kind of speech, and I'm not aware of the fact that the men were taken outside of the school. That's quite simply a lie. If this is what someone has said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you say it was a lie because you've told us that on the -- between the 17th and the 19th of April, you spent a total of approximately 40 to 50 minutes in the presence of any Muslim prisoners over a 72 hour period, 40 to 50 minutes and based upon that, you've expressed all the opinions and said that someone would be lying if a speech was made to prisoners at the school? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the form of the question. The question is argumentative. It assumes facts not in evidence and it in fact twists the words of the witness. The witness answered he did not give a speech. If someone said he gave a speech, that would be a lie. Whether he was there for 40 or 50 minutes or four to five hours, the witness knows whether he personally gave a speech. If the Prosecutor wants to ask the question in a different way, "Are you aware if someone else gave a speech?" That would be a proper question but there question is argumentative, Your Honour, and I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, we did not see the question in your way but any way, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll go on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, did I understand your testimony correctly to say that throughout this period of time, you only saw -- well, let me not ask it that way at the risk of being accused of mischaracterising. Can you just tell us again how many times you saw Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, during this time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I only saw Mr. Naletilic once during that time period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how far away from him were you when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: About three to four metres away from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Naletilic prior to seeing him on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you know of him by reputation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: No. I knew nothing about him up until that day I knew nothing about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask the usher's assistance to show the witness Exhibit P36? If I could ask that could be put, in the interests of time, on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can look at that, sir, and the Chamber will recall the approximate time period of this photo. Can you look at that? Do you see the man that you say you saw one time in Sovici-Doljani, the man you said was Tuta? Do you see him in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes. I can see him now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you take a pointer and point out the one, the man who you think is Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: [indicates] That's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Provided that we will have to then provide a clean copy of that exhibit, but perhaps you can use this extra one, can I ask the usher to hand you a marker and could you please circle and mark with a number 1 the person you've said is Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, sir. Sir, in this photograph, Mr. Tuta doesn't have black hair, does he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Difficult to see in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, the man to Mr. Naletilic's right, other man with glasses, his shirt collar open, what would you say is the colour of his hair? Dark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Who are you referring to? I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know a man named Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you see him in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Which one is he? Can you mark that -- circle his head, please, and mark it number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How did you know Mr. Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NX
utterances.text: I met Mr. Andabak later on, after 1993. I would meet him at various meetings in Mostar and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I'm finished with that exhibit. Thank you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, should we stop here?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll we have been advised that tomorrow morning, there may be some traffic control in the centre of the city, so if anybody lives in the direction of Rotterdam, you had better start your journey before 6.00, otherwise you'll be prevented from entering into the city. So we'll resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 4.27 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 15th day of October, 2002, at 9.30 a.m.
